images.filename: Japanese Center Force ships leave Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944 (NH 63435).jpg
images.caption: Battle of Leyte Gulf, October 1944: The Japanese "Center Force" leaves Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944, en route to the Philippines. Ships are, from right to left: battleships Nagato, Musashi and Yamato; heavy cruisers Maya, Chōkai, Takao, Atago, Haguro and Myōkō.
images.alt: Battle of Leyte Gulf, October 1944: The Japanese "Center Force" leaves Brunei Bay, Borneo, on 22 October 1944, en route to the Philippines. Ships are, from right to left: battleships Nagato, Musashi and Yamato; heavy cruisers Maya, Chōkai, Takao, Atago, Haguro and Myōkō.
categories: Images from the Naval History and Heritage Command

images.caption: Lot-2406-34:  Japanese cruiser Chokai, Atago class, starboard view, 1938. Chokai was scuttled after gunfire/bomb damage in the Battle off Samar, October 25, 1944.   Halftone copy from the files of the Department of Naval Intelligence, June 1943.   Courtesy of the Library of Congress.  (2016/05/12). Silhouette of an Ise-class battleship visible at left. Chokai is alongside Maya (two stripes on the funnel indicate she is the second ship of Sentai 4.

images.caption:
Title: Carrier strike on Rabaul, 5 November 1943
Caption: Japanese ships under carrier plane attack in Simpson Harbor. Cruiser with big fire aft is MAYA (left center). Several other cruisers are among the ships heading for sea, to the right. View looks north, with Rabaul town at top center and Lakunai airfield in top right. Photographed from a USS SARATOGA (CV-3) plane.

images.caption:
Title: Carrier strike on Rabaul, 5 November 1943
Caption: Japanese ships in Simpson Harbor as U.S. carrier planes attack. Several heavy and light cruisers are present. Burning cruiser at left is MAYA. Cruiser with explosion forward, in center, is probably TAKAO. Photographed from a USS SARATOGA (CV-3) TBF. View looks east, with Matupi Island in center and South Daughter crater beyond.
